instruction:
Compare six releases: Ubuntu 22.04 and 24.04 LTS, Debian 12 bookworm and 13 trixie, and Alpine Linux 3.22 and 3.23. Use Ubuntu release-cycle/ESM HTML, https://www.debian.org/releases/bookworm/ and the linked trixie page plus the dated 12 July 2026 LTS handover announcement at https://www.debian.org/News/2026/20260712 for architecture/package limits, and https://alpinelinux.org/releases/. Use www.debian.org HTML for Debian LTS details. Record the research date. Return six rows with original release or branch date, standard/full/main support end, project LTS continuation where applicable, separately labelled subscription/third-party extensions, and the responsible support team where stated. Preserve date precision and expose unresolved source differences. For each release assess scheduled principal-repository security support through 30 June 2027 and 30 June 2028, allowing Debian-project LTS but excluding subscriptions, third-party extensions and discretionary on-request fixes. Give yes, no or boundary/insufficient precision; a month-only deadline matching the horizon is a boundary, while an exact support-through date equal to it qualifies. Calculate runway months from November 2026 to the final qualifying support month using max(0,12*(end year-2026)+(end month-11)), showing inputs. Cite every deadline and verdict. Compare Ubuntu Main/Universe, Debian LTS architecture/package limits and Alpine main/community in three rows. Audit “every Ubuntu package has identical five-year coverage without a subscription” and “Alpine community always shares main’s support end,” then list qualifying releases and boundary cases for both horizons.

Stopping condition: Stop when six lifecycle rows, twelve horizon verdicts, six runway calculations, three scope comparisons, two assertion audits and both qualifying lists are complete.

Constraints:
- Only use the browser actions available to you. Do not open API endpoints, raw data files, view-source pages or downloads, and do not use external programs.
- Do not sign in or create accounts. Do not provide anyone's private personal information; use only task-supplied fictional values if an interaction requests personal details.
- Remain read-only: do not purchase, reserve, apply, post, send messages, contact people or change external records.
- Navigation, search, filtering, sorting and read-only form or calculator interactions are allowed.
- Do not bypass authentication, paywalls, CAPTCHAs or access challenges. Dismiss optional prompts without creating an account or supplying personal information.
- Support the answer with observed page evidence and source URLs. For values that can change, report what the site shows during the run. Preserve the requested dates, units and scope; report unavailable information explicitly instead of inventing it.

items.criterion: Record research date and cite sources
items.description: Evaluate if the agent recorded the current research date and explicitly cited sources/URLs for every deadline and verdict using the specified websites. Full credit if the research date is present and all deadlines/verdicts are accompanied by proper citations, or if the agent clearly reports that the required websites were inaccessible. Partial credit if the research date is missing or citations are incomplete.

items.criterion: Six lifecycle rows for specified releases
items.description: Evaluate if the agent provided 6 rows comparing Ubuntu 22.04, Ubuntu 24.04 LTS, Debian 12 bookworm, Debian 13 trixie, Alpine Linux 3.22, and Alpine Linux 3.23. Each row must include: original release/branch date, standard/full/main support end, project LTS continuation (where applicable), separately labelled subscription/third-party extensions, and responsible support team where stated. Full credit if all 6 rows are present with all required fields, preserving date precision and exposing unresolved source differences (e.g., for future unannounced dates or missing information), or if the agent clearly reports site inaccessibility. Deduct 1 point for each missing or incomplete row when data was accessible.

Evaluate if the agent assessed principal-repository security support for all 6 releases through 30 June 2027 and 30 June 2028 (12 verdicts total). Verdicts must allow Debian-project LTS but exclude subscriptions, third-party extensions and discretionary on-request fixes, yielding 'yes', 'no', or 'boundary/insufficient precision'. Full credit if all 12 verdicts are present and correctly follow the exclusion rules based on the available data, or if missing data is properly attributed to missing site info or inaccessibility. Partial credit scaled based on the number of correct and present verdicts (0.5 points per verdict). A month-only deadline matching the horizon is a boundary; an exact support-through date equal to the horizon qualifies.

Evaluate if the agent calculated the runway months from November 2026 to the final qualifying support month for all 6 releases using the formula max(0, 12*(end year-2026) + (end month-11)), and explicitly showed the inputs. Full credit if all 6 calculations are correct based on the dates found (even if the dates themselves were 'insufficient precision', provided the math logic is sound and inputs are shown), or if calculation was impossible due to reported site inaccessibility. Deduct 1 point for each missing or incorrect calculation/input display.

Evaluate if the agent provided three rows comparing: 1) Ubuntu Main vs Universe, 2) Debian LTS architecture and package limits, and 3) Alpine main vs community. Full credit if all 3 comparisons are present and accurately reflect the support scope limits based on the sources, or if missing due to reported site inaccessibility. Partial credit (1 point per correct comparison row).

Evaluate if the agent audited the assertion: 'every Ubuntu package has identical five-year coverage without a subscription'. Full credit if the agent correctly addresses this assertion based on the Main vs. Universe repository differences found on the site, or if the Ubuntu site was inaccessible and this was explicitly reported.

Evaluate if the agent audited the assertion: 'Alpine community always shares main's support end'. Full credit if the agent correctly addresses this assertion by pointing out the actual lifecycle differences between Alpine's main and community repositories based on the site, or if the Alpine site was inaccessible and this was explicitly reported.

items.criterion: List qualifying releases and boundary cases for both horizons
items.description: Evaluate if the agent listed the qualifying releases and boundary cases for both the 30 June 2027 and 30 June 2028 horizons. Full credit if both lists are complete and correctly summarize the horizon verdicts derived from the extracted data, or if omitted strictly due to reported site inaccessibility. Partial credit if only one horizon's list is provided or if there are minor omissions.
